title: Three-tier decision tree for advisory requests (scoring + routing + SLA defaults)
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers submit optimization/advisory requests (batching, KV/prefix caching, quantization profiles, routing policies) with highly variable signal. We need a deterministic, SLA-aware intake and prioritization flow that converts raw requests into: 1) self-serve guidance, 2) a scoped advisory engagement, or 3) an urgent engineering runway for regressions.

Goal: Deliver a three-tier decision tree that judges requests by business impact, complexity, and reproducibility and routes them to the right lane (Self-Serve, Concierge Advisory, Engineering Runbook) with default SLA and response expectations. The output will be a triage microservice spec + scoring rubric + playbook docs for support/solutions/eng teams.

Scope: PM-owned intake rubric (scoring thresholds), routing defaults for Dedicated/Hosted/Private customers, escalations for regressions or SLO breaches, and standard artifact links (eval sets, sample payloads, A/B plan). Not in scope right now: enforcement automation in the console (separate follow-up).

Success metrics: median time-to-first-response by lane (target Self-Serve<24h, Concierge<3d, Engineering runway<5d), % of requests resolved without engineering changes, and customer satisfaction (CSAT) for advisory outcomes.
comments: 2026-03-02 — PM kickoff: scoped deliverables, aligned with Support and Solutions. Agreed to base scoring on 3 axes: customer business impact, reproducibility effort, and infra risk.

2026-03-06 — Draft rubric v0 posted: weights proposed (impact 40%, reproducibility 30%, infra risk 30%). Feedback from Solutions: add a separate gate for security/compliance requests.

2026-03-08 — Design review with Console PM: suggested a minimal intake form with discrete fields (model, deployment type, observed latency/cost delta, sample prompt). Action: design to prototype form by 2026-03-15.
2026-03-10 — Engineering sync: ENG requested that we include a field for "estimated tokens/sec" and whether KV cache is used. They flagged dependency ENG-8942 for autoscaling telemetry.

2026-03-12 — Scoring thresholds agreed in working group: Self-Serve <= 20 score, Concierge 21-55, Engineering >55. Draft playbook pages created for each lane. Assigned follow-ups for playbook QA and runbook links.
